scores.evidence: Phase 1 "Depends on: V0 passes"; "Phase 2 Depends on: Phase 1 exit check and V1 pass"
scores.rationale: Phases run substrate (skeleton, build infra, secrets, observability) to deployment safety to onboarding to scale, each gated by a validation; the dependency map is somewhat muddled but the ordering holds.

scores.evidence: "One real microservice (canary service) ... passes through the new platform from commit to production within the latency targets, with a rollback verified."
scores.rationale: Phase 0 is a real end-to-end commit-to-production path with rollback, observability and a concrete exit check.

scores.evidence: "If p95 latency > 8 min, split fast and slow test tiers"; build-vs-buy default with R3 reversibility and flip conditions
scores.rationale: A table of irreversible decisions gives defaults, assumptions, validation and flip conditions, and assumptions are labeled.

scores.evidence: "Orchestration platform baseline (widest rework if wrong)"; "Onboard 3 lowest-risk services" then larger waves
scores.rationale: Tasks are explicitly ordered with the widest-impact work first in each phase, and exposure grows from small to large.

scores.evidence: "webhook from GitHub uses HMAC-SHA256 signature verification"; per-phase security column through Phase 4
scores.rationale: Concrete security work appears in every phase from Phase 0 (secret injection, webhook verification, access limits) onward.

scores.evidence: "All platform and service logs routed to central log aggregator ... searchable within 2 s"
scores.rationale: Phase 0 has concrete logging, dashboards and alerts, and every later phase extends them.

scores.evidence: "immutable base image (digest pinned, not tag); build cache versioned with Dockerfile"
scores.rationale: Reproducibility measures (digest pinning, content addressing, version-controlled manifests, commit-mapped deploys) appear in every phase.

scores.evidence: "Automated: if service error rate > 5% ... kill canary traffic and revert to previous image."
scores.rationale: Rollback is in Phase 0, and backup/restore, DR drills, fallback pipelines and incident drills follow in later phases.

scores.evidence: "N/A — no AI component. This is a traditional CI/CD orchestration platform, not an agentic system."
scores.rationale: The plan explicitly declares the AI layer N/A and adds no AI components.

scores.evidence: "Multi-region deployment: Deferred to Phase 4. Condition: trigger if a) single-region outage > 4 hours observed..."
scores.rationale: A deferred-work list gives explicit triggers for each item, though a couple of triggers are vague.

note: A strong, well-threaded plan with a real Phase 0 skeleton, explicit gates and deferrals, and the AI layer correctly marked N/A. Minor flaws are a muddled dependency map, Phase 0 running on hardened-later defaults, and some inconsistencies.
